label: Copy-phase/delimiter steps whose input is w, r, a, t, k, o, i or <DEL>
explanation: Fires almost only at the delimiter and during the copy phase: 99% of activation mass is at t >= L, and it almost never fires on the original tokens (it is silent at t=0). Inside that window it depends on the input token: w, r, a, t and <DEL> have the highest rates (15-19%), then k, o, i (about 8%). Out_tok (k, o, n, w highest) and next_out (1, f, q, h highest) also raise the rate. Recall is highest at the delimiter and at recall_idx 0-4, which mostly reflects longer sequences, and is lowest on the final output step. The largest activations (about 0.9-1.0 of max) come on copy-phase inputs such as r, w, k or a that are followed by o, k or r. The code is spread across tokens: no simple combination of in_tok, out_tok and next_out gets past roughly 0.39 F1 on dev. This predicate keeps about 83% of the mass, but precision is only about 0.22, because most copy steps with these inputs stay below threshold.
